thread: Copied yard marks on tainted shipments, and Corin's unanswered letters to Dalaran

evidence.clue: The inspection office keeps the second copy of every bill that leaves under a yard's mark. Fenner's mark for the south road is a hook with two bars through the shank; Fenner's clerk starts the hook at the top and pulls it down; the copied one was started at the bottom, with a dark bead where the pen rested. On the day of the bill Fenner's own book has both its south wagons in the shed with a cracked axle.

Forty-one copied bills Corin will swear to since midsummer (Fenner's, the Exchange, Garside's marks); mostly the south road, some the weir road and the east road. When a village sickens the reeve writes to the town and the letter comes to the inspection office; some villages on copied marks have since written in sick, the rest 'haven't yet'.
Sample-room readings (Jaina): every bag on a copied mark is heavy; bags on true marks are clean. A column in Corin's hand: Heavy. Heavy. Clean. Heavy. Heavy., with the hook beside each.
Corin wrote weekly to the Citadel inspection desk from the first copied mark, then to the Archmage's secretary; kept copies; never got an answer. 'Nobody's coming' from Dalaran.
Kett's bills are all written for the first carts out (south and weir roads); Kett keeps nothing overnight.

readerKnows: The poison ships under copied marks of three yards; Dalaran's inspection channel went silent for a summer.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas and Jaina: the marks are being copied and the bags match; Corin's paper is credible. Nobody knows who copies them.
notes: Do not resolve who copies the marks. Havel's reading of it ('I can't arrest a village') is local caution, not guilt. The inspection copies prove the pattern; the sample-room bags prove the contents.
